EXAFS spectra and fitting results revealed a complex local structure composed of both Co-O and Co-Co pathways, which closely resembles Co3O4.

Co 2p XPS spectra displayed two doublets arising from spin-orbit coupling and two satellite peaks. Peaks at 780.6 and 796.8 eV corresponding to Co3+ 2p3/2 and 2p1/2, signals at 783.3 and 798.5 eV assigned to Co2+ 2p3/2 and 2p1/2. No signal at 778.1 eV corresponding to metallic Co0.

WT-EXAFS spectral analysis confirmed the coexistence of Co-O and Co-O-Co linkages (Co3O4). A strong intensity maximum at low R (~2.0 Å) and moderate k-values (~4-8 Å-1) corresponds to Co-O scattering, while a broader signal at higher R (~3.0 Å) and k (~8-10 Å-1) reflects the Co-O-Co linkages.

UV-vis DRS revealed a broad absorption band between 330 and 480 nm, assigned to CoOx oligomers, a weak peak at ~520 nm attributed to a small fraction of isolated Co2+ species, and a distinct absorption band at 720 nm characteristic of ligand-to-metal charge transfer (O2-→Co3+) in spinel Co3O4, indicating Co3O4 is the predominant cobalt phase.
Normalized Co K-edge XANES spectrum exhibited a well-defined white-line peak at approximately 7729.0 eV, positioned between those of CoO (Co2+) and Co2O3 (Co3+), indicating a mixed-valence state.
